fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Access Road; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of obstructions at all times could significantly improve emergency vehicle entry and exit, particularly given the presence of multiple structures on the property. Marking or maintaining visible address identification near the street frontage may assist responding units in locating the property quickly. Where dense vegetation borders the driveway or approaches to either structure, periodic management of that growth could improve visibility and maneuvering room for larger emergency vehicles. Identifying and communicating any secondary access pathway to the rear of the property with local emergency services may support more effective staging and operational flexibility during a response.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Dense Shrub Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Fuel Continuity; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Brushland Interface; Limited Defensible Space; Vegetated Access Route; Heavy Brush
wildfire.recommendations: Managing vegetation in the immediate vicinity of the structure should be a primary focus, as reducing the concentration of shrubs and woody fuels within and around the structure perimeter could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity. Where vegetation is directly adjacent to or surrounding the structure, creating separation between plants and combustible surfaces — including walls, eaves, decks, and fences — may reduce structure exposure and support suppression operations. Thinning or spacing out shrub masses and vegetation clusters on the property could reduce the opportunity for fire to move continuously from the surrounding brushland interface toward the structure. Maintaining the access route by managing encroaching vegetation along the driveway or entry road would support firefighter access and improve evacuation conditions. Periodic ongoing management of mixed vegetation cover across the property, rather than a single clearing effort, would support long-term wildfire resilience and help sustain the defensible space over time.
